title: Sex life: I believe that roleplay can be healing
gist: Sydney sex worker Tilly Lawless argues that taboo roleplay bookings are frequently therapeutic rather than deviant — clients often re-enact abuse from a position of power to regain autonomy — while candidly noting that consensual non-consent did nothing for her own trauma even as an unrelated roleplay ended a decade of nightmares. She adds a practical observation that first-time elaborate fantasies usually disappoint, and that the most sophisticated clients built their desires slowly rather than importing them ready-made from porn or manga.

insights.claim: Sexual roleplay carries healing potential because it lets participants act out or rewrite past events, from sexual trauma to taboo attraction, rather than merely offering escapism or variety.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: Reframes commercial sexual services as adjacent to therapeutic practice — relevant to how regulation and destigmatisation debates around sex work are argued.
insights.quote: I also think roleplay has healing potential, as it offers the opportunity to act out or rewrite past events in life, from sexual trauma to taboo attraction.
insights.locator: I’ve written before about why I enjoy roleplay bookings

insights.claim: People who seek out taboo roleplays are often themselves victims of sexual abuse who want to relive that experience from a position of power, using the scenario to regain some autonomy.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: Undercuts the assumption that taboo demand signals predatory intent — the causal story runs from prior victimhood to fantasy, not the reverse.
insights.quote: A person may be seeking out a specific roleplay because they have been a victim of sexual abuse themselves and wish to relive that experience from a position of power.

insights.claim: The ethical test for a sexual roleplay should be whether it brings solace and release while hurting no one, not whether outside observers find the scenario morally comfortable.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: A clean harm-principle framing that maps onto wider culture-war arguments about regulating private consensual behaviour.

themes.theme: The age-play objection and its rebuttal

insights.claim: Clients who ask a woman in her thirties to play a seduced teenage girl could legally book an actual 18-year-old instead, and pointing this out makes objectors reconsider their reading of the fantasy.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: The revealed-preference argument — paying more for simulation over legal reality — is the strongest available defence of taboo roleplay in public debate.
insights.quote: When I point out that my clients could choose to legally book an 18-year-old girl if they wanted, and instead book me, a woman in my thirties, they often reconsider.

themes.theme: Where the therapeutic claim breaks down

insights.claim: Consensual non-consent, or rapeplay, did not alter this sex worker's own relationship with past assaults or lessen her fear of future assault, even when practised with trusted partners and long-standing clients.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: An honest counterexample from an advocate — the healing thesis is probabilistic, not a mechanism that reliably fires.
insights.quote: I never found it altered my relationship with past assaults or lessened my fear of future assault.
insights.locator: Whilst I have enjoyed rapeplay with partners

insights.claim: An unplanned roleplay requested by a long-term regular client released the author from repeated nightmares she had had for over a decade, an effect she never predicted.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: Suggests therapeutic benefit arrives unpredictably and outside the scenarios explicitly designed to address trauma.
insights.quote: acting out his fantasy of taboo sexual relations freed me from repeated nightmares I’d had for over a decade

insights.claim: A young client who paid to re-enact losing his virginity to a popular girl from his school bus described the experience afterwards as underwhelming because he had expected to climax more times than he did.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: Illustrates the expectation gap that drives churn and dissatisfaction in any experience-purchase market built on fantasy.

insights.claim: Fantasies are often best left in the imagination because real-life execution rarely lives up to the mental version, and first-timers routinely attempt too much.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: A general expectation-management principle: elaborate first attempts under-deliver relative to simpler ones.

insights.claim: Clients with the most complex sexual fantasies built them slowly over years of experimentation, rather than arriving with a ready-made, one-size-fits-all script imported from porn or manga.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: Cuts against the simple 'porn shapes desire' narrative — media supplies scripts to novices, while durable preferences are built through iteration.

insights.claim: Highly specific roleplay requests are a marker of self-knowledge, indicating someone who has reckoned directly with desires and trauma that others keep in the shadows.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: Inverts the stigma gradient: specificity reads as psychological work done, not pathology.
insights.quote: To me, these people have reckoned directly with what others may keep in the shadows, including trauma.
